actions.action: Show an outcome for every file
actions.mechanism: Per-file states distinguish accepted receipts, definite failures, pending uploads, and outcomes that remain unknown.
actions.implementation: Render five attachment slots with filename, text status, and relevant controls. Mark acceptance only after receiving a stable server receipt.
actions.check: Simulate two acceptances, two failures, and one timeout; verify each has the correct status and next step.
actions.risk: A timeout must not appear as a definite rejection.

actions.action: Retry only files that need another upload
actions.mechanism: Selective retry preserves accepted receipts instead of restarting the entire batch or resubmitting the form.
actions.implementation: Offer individual retry and “Retry failed files.” Reuse in-memory files while available; otherwise request reselection. Exclude accepted and unresolved entries.
actions.check: Fail three of five uploads, then retry; network logs must show no retransmission of the two accepted files.
actions.risk: Reselected files may differ; require users to confirm replacements.

actions.action: Resolve uncertain outcomes before offering another upload
actions.mechanism: Receipt reconciliation distinguishes a lost response from an upload the server never accepted.
actions.implementation: Add anonymous, scoped upload-attempt lookup around existing processing. Associate attempt tokens with resulting receipts; after timeout, query before enabling retry.
actions.check: Drop an acceptance response; reconciliation must recover its receipt without retransmitting bytes. Unresolved attempts must remain visibly unresolved.
actions.risk: Requires coordination metadata, not changes to file processing.

actions.action: Explain recovery when the tab reopens
actions.mechanism: Receipt-based restoration recovers accepted attachments without retaining file bytes or pretending failed selections remain available.
actions.implementation: Persist only opaque receipts with a 24-hour lifetime. Resolve valid receipts into attachment rows; explain that unfinished selections require reselection. Discard expired recovery entries.
actions.check: Close after partial acceptance and reopen: accepted files return without uploads; missing selections are explained. Expired receipts cannot restore the browser draft.
actions.risk: Unavailable storage or cleared receipts prevents automatic recovery.

actions.mechanism: Attachment slots separate user intent from upload completion, preventing late responses from undoing removal or exceeding five files.
actions.implementation: Give each slot a version. Replacing or removing invalidates that version; ignore late results for the final list. Count pending slots toward five.
actions.check: Remove a pending file, add its replacement, then deliver the old receipt; the removed attachment must stay excluded.
actions.risk: Excluding a receipt does not imply deleting its server file.

actions.action: Require review of the exact final list
actions.mechanism: A separate review checkpoint prevents unresolved or silently omitted attachments from becoming an accidental final submission.
actions.implementation: Show the ordered accepted attachment list and count. Require explicit exclusion of unresolved entries and final confirmation; invalidate confirmation whenever attachments change.
actions.check: Change an attachment after reviewing: submission must require review again. An unresolved entry must block submission until resolved or explicitly excluded.
actions.risk: Do not imply that reviewing names verifies file contents.

actions.action: Make repeated case submission recover the same case
actions.mechanism: Atomic finalization makes double-clicks and lost submission responses return an existing case rather than create duplicates.
actions.implementation: Group upload receipts under an anonymous draft. Finalize that draft once; repeated finalization returns its case receipt. Receipt recovery also reports whether submission already completed.
actions.check: Send concurrent submissions and drop the first response; retry and reopen must identify one case, without uploading accepted files again.
actions.risk: Requires case-creation coordination and securely scoped anonymous recovery.
